note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Is this pump throttled by a control valve when it could run on a variable speed drive?

evidence.text: equipment CND-PU-162 (asset S2-PU001) reads "CND-PU-162 CONDENSATE PUMP" on sheet 2
valve FCV-1621 (asset S2-IN022) on sheet 2 at CND-HTR-161 (by the extraction's attribution)
instrument FIT-16299 (asset S2-IN015) on sheet 2 at CND-PU-162 (by the extraction's attribution)
instrument FO-1621 (asset S2-IN018) on sheet 2 at CND-PU-162 (by the extraction's attribution)
instrument FT-XXX (asset S2-IN019) [placeholder tag on the drawing] on sheet 2 at CND-PU-162 (by the extraction's attribution)
instrument FIT-163101 (asset S2-IN020) on sheet 2 at CND-PU-163 (by the extraction's attribution)
instrument FIT-164102 (asset S2-IN021) on sheet 2 at CND-PU-164 (by the extraction's attribution)
no speed control (SC, SIC, SY tag, VFD or VSD) on or next to the pump
the extracted links have no recorded flow direction, so 'near' means within the stated number of drawn links on the same sheet; which side of the equipment it is on is not established by the model

data_requests.item: Control valve position (% open) over normal operation
where: historian or DCS trend for FCV-1621 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: the valve's controller output
a walkdown: read the positioner stroke indicator at several rates
data_requests.how: Take a month or more of valve output at normal sampling; note the typical and the lowest % open, and the hours at each.

data_requests.item: Flow over the same period (a flow-duration curve)
where: historian or DCS trend for FIT-16299, FIT-163101, FIT-164102, FO-1621, FT-XXX (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
site records: production rate records
data_requests.how: Bin the flow into ranges and count the hours in each.

where: the blank CAPACITY field on the sheet 2 equipment schedule, entry CND-PU-162
the blank DISCHARGE field on the sheet 2 equipment schedule, entry CND-PU-162
the vendor datasheet: pump curve and rated duty point
the pump nameplate on CND-PU-162
data_requests.how: Copy the rated flow and head and get the pump curve.

where: the blank HP field on the sheet 2 equipment schedule, entry CND-PU-162
the blank RPM field on the sheet 2 equipment schedule, entry CND-PU-162
the motor nameplate on CND-PU-162
maintenance records: motor record card
data_requests.how: Copy rated power, speed and efficiency from the motor nameplate.

where: a walkdown: elevations and pressures at the suction source and the delivery point
site records: line list or isometrics for pipe lengths and sizes
data_requests.how: Static head = lift plus pressure difference between source and destination; the rest of the pump head at duty is friction plus the valve drop.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a drive quote when the valve normally runs well throttled for long hours and most of the head is friction rather than static lift (VSDs suit friction-dominated systems best). Close it if the valve normally runs near fully open, the head is mostly static, or the pump runs few hours.

typical_benefit.wording: "With rotodynamic pump installations, savings of between 30% and 50% have been achieved in many installations by installing VSDs." Also: "It is estimated that 75% of pump systems are oversized, many by more than 20%."
typical_benefit.arc: 2.4146 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 5,227 recommendations, 3.0 yr average payback, 31.4% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S15: Variable Speed Pumping: A Guide to Successful Applications, Executive Summary (DOE ITP with Europump/HI, DOE/GO-102004-1913, May 2004)

questions.question: Is this motor oversized for its load?

evidence.text: equipment ACC-PU-151 (asset S1-PU013) reads "ACC-PU-151 AIR COOLED CONDENSER PUMP" on sheet 1

where: the blank HP field on the sheet 1 equipment schedule, entry ACC-PU-151
the motor nameplate on ACC-PU-151
maintenance records: motor record card
data_requests.how: Copy rated power, full-load amps and efficiency.

data_requests.item: Measured input power or current at normal load
where: a walkdown: a clamp-on power meter (or ammeter plus voltage) at the motor starter
data_requests.how: Measure kW (or amps and volts) over a typical period.

questions.decision_rule: Load factor = measured input power divided by (rated output divided by rated efficiency). A motor running well below about 40% of full load is worth a resize question; one oversized slightly is fine.

typical_benefit.wording: "At loads below 40% of full load, motor efficiency begins to decline dramatically." "Slightly oversizing a motor (up to 25%) can actually increase efficiency." No % saving stated.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.41xx (category only) (IAC/ITAC browse page: motors: 18,002 recommendations, 2.5 yr average payback, 52.3% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S16: Improving Motor and Drive System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry (DOE/GO-102014-4356, Feb 2014; prepared by WSU Energy Program + NREL)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: Fires only where the drawing carries a motor rating field (filled or blank); a drawing without one gives no trigger. IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.

questions.question: Is high-grade steam let down, bypassed or desuperheated for a duty a lower grade could serve?

evidence.text: equipment ESS-HTR-180 (asset S4-TK001) reads "ESS-HTR-180 DE SUPERHEATER" on sheet 4
valve TCV-16013 (asset S4-IN001) on sheet 4 at ESS-HTR-180 (by the extraction's attribution)
valve FCV-18012 (asset S4-IN014) on sheet 4 at ESS-HTR-180 (by the extraction's attribution)
valve PCV-14011 (asset S4-IN016) on sheet 4 at ESS-HTR-180 (by the extraction's attribution)
offpage "MSS PID 140-1 PEGGING STEAM" (S4-OP005) on sheet 4 at ESS-HTR-180 (by the extraction's attribution)
offpage "CND PID 160-1 (E-1) CONDENSATE SYSTEM" (S4-OP001) on sheet 4 at ESS-HTR-180 (by the extraction's attribution)

data_requests.item: Steam flow through the station, with hours
where: only a valve (FCV-18012, PCV-14011, TCV-16013) is drawn on this line, with no flow measurement; flow needs a meter or a calibrated valve curve
site records: steam balance
data_requests.how: Build a flow-duration curve: how many hours at each flow.

data_requests.item: Upstream and downstream pressure and temperature
where: a walkdown: gauges and thermometers either side of the station
site records: header design conditions
data_requests.how: Record at normal operation.

where: the blank CAPACITY field on the sheet 4 equipment schedule, entry ESS-HTR-180
the vendor datasheet: station or desuperheater datasheet
data_requests.how: Copy rated flow.

where: site records: operating procedures: startup, trip, normal duty
data_requests.how: Mark the station startup-only, trip-only or normal duty.

questions.decision_rule: If the station passes steam only at startup or trips, close this screening investigation; this is not an instruction to operate the station. If it passes steady flow in normal duty, ask whether a lower-grade source (an extraction or exhaust at the right pressure) could serve the user, or whether the pressure drop could do work: S6's condition for a backpressure turbogenerator is a constant flow of at least 3,000 lb/hr and a drop of at least 100 psi.

typical_benefit.wording: Closest source wording (for the pressure-reducing part, S6): consider a backpressure turbogenerator when a PRV has "constant steam flows of at least 3,000 pounds per hour (lb/hr), and when the steam pressure drop is at least 100 psi." No source found with a number for desuperheater or bypass stations themselves.
source_titles: S6: Steam Tip #20, Replace Pressure-Reducing Valves with Backpressure Turbogenerators (DOE/GO-102012-3409)

questions.limits: Turbine bypass and pegging stations exist for startup, trips and low load; the question is only about hours of normal-duty flow.
